solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wanting to drop off old coins, carrying burden

indicators.note: the old coins are said to carry the burden, so it sits inside them

parts.note: sous were old French coins of small value
lumber is a heavy load or encumbrance, as in being lumbered with something

explanation.surface: Someone is too weighed down by a bag of old coins to nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wanting to drop off' looks like a wish to let go of the coins; it means feeling drowsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sleepy, inclined to nod off, can be described with this literary adjective.

clue.text: Drop of beer knocked back

indicators.note: a drink knocked back is downed, and here the word for the beer runs backwards

parts.note: pils is a short name for Pilsner lager

explanation.surface: A drinker downs the last drop of lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' reads as drinking; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a fall or tumble, so as a noun it matches a drop in level or footing.

clue.text: Rises in pressure routine in America

indicators.note: the second 'in' puts the pressure and routine pieces inside the abbreviation for America

parts.note: US is short for the United States
P is the physics symbol for pressure
a turn is a performer's routine or act

explanation.surface: A report on climbing pressure in some American procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Upturns are upward movements, improvements or increases, matching rises as plural nouns.

clue.text: E.g. Bradbury with an innovative story

indicators.note: something innovative is made new, so these letters are given a fresh order

parts.note: the abbreviation contributes its two letters E and G

explanation.surface: Ray Bradbury, the science-fiction author, offered as an example of a writer with an original tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'innovative' signal rearranges EG, BRADBURY and AN together.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is a novel by Charles Dickens, so it is an example of a story.

clue.text: Catch sun by desert palm

parts.note: to rat on someone is to desert or betray them
to catch the sun is to get a tan

explanation.surface: Getting sunburnt next to a palm tree in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' wants to be a sandy place; it is the verb, to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Rattan is a climbing palm whose stems are used for cane furniture.

clue.text: Without order, entity lazily moves one three places back

indicators.note: the letter for one is shifted within the joined words rather than staying put
the shifted letter travels three positions towards the end of the word

parts.note: a unit is a single thing or entity
to act idly is to act lazily
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lazy creature slowly shuffles backwards in a messy way.
explanation.walkthrough: UNIT plus IDLY gives UNITIDLY; 'moves' with 'three places back' carries its first I three positions along.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a messy, disorganised way is doing it without order.

clue.text: Mrs Norman, say, rebuffed a title

indicators.note: something rebuffed is pushed back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a Norman spoke French, and Mme, Madame, is the French form of Mrs

explanation.surface: A married woman refuses to accept a title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Title' looks like a rank; it is the name of a book, Jane Austen's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is the name of a Jane Austen novel, so it is a book's title.

clue.text: Big Eddy's out of line and ultimately lacking genius

indicators.note: the word is left without its last letter
the line letter is taken out of the whirlpool word

parts.note: a maelstrom is a huge whirlpool, a big eddy of water

explanation.surface: A man called Big Eddy, a misfit who is no genius.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big Eddy' looks like a nickname; it is a whirlpool. 'Out of' removes L and 'ultimately lacking' drops the final M.
explanation.definitionFit: A maestro is a master of an art, especially music, a person of great talent.

clue.text: Mostly criminal men punching mug or suckers

indicators.note: the inner pieces strike into the middle of the fool's word

parts.note: a mug is a fool or dupe, an ass

indicators.note: most of the word is kept, its final letter lost

parts.note: a pirate is a criminal of the seas
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers or men

explanation.surface: Criminal men mugging and punching someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' reads as a verb for robbery; it is a fool, ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspirators are devices that draw out fluid or air by suction, things that suck.

clue.text: Lacking will to embrace right American way

indicators.note: the will-less word holds the letter for right in its arms

parts.note: someone intestate died without making a will

explanation.surface: Without determination, a person fails to embrace the correct American path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' looks like determination; it is a legal testament.
explanation.definitionFit: An interstate is a US highway linking states, so it is an American road.

clue.text: Look the wrong way for honour

indicators.note: reading a word the wrong way means reading it backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: Glancing in the wrong direction while seeking honour.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a promise is to honour it, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Assumed warmth's from part of bulb around high piece of wood

indicators.note: the garlic piece is wrapped around the other two pieces

parts.note: a clove is one segment of a garlic bulb
up means high, as in up in the air
a board is a flat piece of timber

explanation.surface: Looks like a gardening instruction about bulbs and a raised plank of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light bulb or a flower; it is garlic. The 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupboard love is affection shown only to get something, such as food, so the warmth is feigned.

clue.text: Subsistence in lodgings containing study, say

indicators.note: the lodgings word holds the study word inside it

parts.note: a B and B, bed and breakfast, is cheap lodging
to read a subject is to study it at university
to utter is to say

explanation.surface: Someone renting a room while studying, scraping a living.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Study, say' looks like an example; 'say' is its own piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread and butter means one's basic living or livelihood, the means of getting by.

clue.text: Free agent returned letter

indicators.note: something returned comes back, so the agent word runs backwards

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A spy sends back a letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' looks like a single alphabet character; it is correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Permissive means allowing freedom, liberal and tolerant, so free fits as an adjective.

clue.text: Some fantasy, as seen from the right texts

indicators.note: reading from the right means right to left, against normal order
only some of the letters of these words are taken

explanation.surface: Fantasy fiction as viewed by right-wing readers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'From the right' looks political; it reverses the letters 'Some' picks out.
explanation.definitionFit: Essays are short written compositions, pieces of writing or texts.

clue.text: Stick with Labour leader? It's a problem for member

parts.note: a club is a heavy stick
Michael Foot led the British Labour Party from 1980 to 1983

explanation.surface: Sticking by the head of the Labour Party causes difficulty for a party member.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Member' reads as a party member; it is a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: A deformed foot is a disability affecting a limb, and member is an old word for limb.

clue.text: Ditch royal bearer of food

parts.note: a trench is a long ditch
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen's royal cipher

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the royal servant who carries the meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ditch' looks like a verb, to discard; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A trencher was a wooden plate or board on which food was served.

clue.text: Irregular army tour departed here?

indicators.note: irregular means not in proper order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A band of irregular soldiers on tour set off from this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Departed' looks like a verb of leaving; it means the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: A morgue is where the bodies of the dead are kept, so the departed lie there.

clue.text: Style so retro for male with comb

indicators.note: to style is to arrange or fashion, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A man styling his hair in a retro way with a comb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comb' looks like a hair comb; it is the fleshy crest on a bird's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cock bird has a red crest called a comb, so it is a male with comb.

clue.text: Hesitate to accept current surrender

indicators.note: the hesitation word takes in the current letter

parts.note: to waver is to hesitate
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Dithering over whether to accept the latest capitulation.
explanation.definitionFit: A waiver is the formal giving up or relinquishing of a right or claim.

clue.text: Bland individual wholly bowled over by avant-garde

parts.note: the van is the vanguard, the leading edge
I, the Roman one, stands for an individual

indicators.note: knocked flat and turned head over heels, so the word for wholly runs backwards

parts.note: all means wholly

explanation.surface: A dull person is completely overwhelmed by experimental art.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowled over' looks like amazement; it reverses ALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanilla is used to mean plain, ordinary and unexciting.

clue.text: Something very sugary has little pastry

parts.note: wee is Scottish for little
a pie is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: A tiny tart loaded with sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sugary' looks like sweet food; it means sentimental.
explanation.definitionFit: A weepie is a sentimental film or story meant to make people cry, so it is saccharine.

clue.text: Belated attempt to raise legitimate issue?

definitions.text: Belated attempt to raise legitimate issue?

parts.words: Belated attempt to raise legitimate issue?
parts.note: a marriage rushed through when a baby is already on the way makes the child born legitimate

explanation.surface: Someone raises a lawful matter too late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' looks like a matter for debate; it means offspring. 'Raise' means bring up a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A forced marriage held because the bride is pregnant, so the child is born in wedlock.

clue.text: Reversal of current change

indicators.note: the word for a current is read backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: A change that turns back the present trend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like an adjective meaning present; it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to revise or alter it.

clue.text: A fan of eastern religion wanting silence

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the silence letters are removed

parts.note: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan
sh is the call for silence

explanation.surface: A follower of an Eastern faith who longs for quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fan of' reads as a person; it is the idiom, as in being keen on something.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something means being enthusiastic about it, a fan of it.

clue.text: In Slough, swimming pool is the worse for use

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed in the cast-off word

parts.note: to slough a skin is to shed it

indicators.note: swimming suggests moving about, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A run-down public swimming pool in the town of Slough, west of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is an English town, but here it is the verb, to shed skin. 'Swimming' rearranges POOL IS into OPSOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods that are shopsoiled are slightly damaged or dirty from being on display.

clue.text: Bring in pot that's picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: an urn is a pot or vase

explanation.surface: Fetching in a pot that has been lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' looks like lifting; it means heard. In British speech the two words rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn money is to bring it in as income.

clue.text: Impertinent rogue never associated with trial

indicators.note: rogue means behaving unpredictably, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheeky rascal who has never been on trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Impertinent' looks like rude; it means not pertinent.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally not pertinent, beside the point, having nothing to do with the matter.
